guides.content:
# Working on mlspend

Use Python 3.12 and the dependencies in pyproject.toml. Run `uv sync --group dev`, `uv run pytest --cov=packages`, `uv run ruff check .`, and `uv run mypy packages`. If the environment blocks local sockets, record that limitation and select the core, method, pipeline, source and direct storage tests explicitly. Do not report that subset as a complete suite pass.

Keep money in Decimal at boundaries and integer microdollars in stored telemetry. Never claim observed usage or current prices from a fixture. Preserve the distinction between simulated cost, shadow cost and actual charges.

Do not edit locked prices, source locks, evaluation registration or generated results by hand. The first initialization uses the registration and fetch commands. Later changes use an explicit new version and explain the reason. Render documents from the manifest. A missing source is a missing source, never zero usage.

The simulator writes truth separately. Only evaluation may load truth. Method modules must use observed telemetry only. Run the import boundary test after changing methods.

Before release, run the local build twice and compare digests, then run the external checks. A skipped check is not a pass. Do not tag a complete release while any mandatory requirement in RESULTS.md is not done.

The expanded implementation is registered in evaluation/v2/plan.json. Run `uv run python -m scripts.build_expanded` for the contracted full-year study and `uv run python -m packages.render.expanded` for its public claims. Run `uv run python -m scripts.check_expanded_reproducibility` for independent process rebuilds with different hash seeds. The earlier study remains preserved for provenance.

Use `.claude/skills/add-a-price-source`, `add-a-cost-rule` and `explain-a-bill` for their named tasks. Validate all three with skills-ref. Run notebooks with `uv run pytest --nbmake notebooks`. The playbook renders these repository instructions.

Protect uv.lock, web/package-lock.json, all source locks and price books, evaluation registrations, sealed truth and results promoted from Actions. Use dependency tooling, explicit source promotion or deterministic rendering to change them. Never silently alter a source artifact or a threshold after looking at holdout results.

Run `uv run python -m scripts.check_diff` on staged or committed changes before publication. It checks added text for credentials and private identifiers. The pre-push hook runs the same check. Review the full renderer, registration, statement, price-lock, vocabulary, palette and method-boundary gates in CI. Missing input to a gate fails closed.

Use the migration credential for `uv run alembic upgrade head`; the runtime role must not create tables. Period-close needs explicit complete actuals and a separate writer credential. Never log or commit database URLs with passwords. An unavailable future actual remains pending rather than becoming zero.

---
name: add-a-price-source
description: Add or update a public pricing source in MLSpend, including a provider fetch, normalization, provenance and lock promotion.
---

# Add A Price Source

Read AGENTS.md and packages/prices/book.py. Write a committed fetch request with exact SKU, region, unit, currency and term. Fetch in Actions with bounded retries and preserved raw bytes. Normalize Decimal rates without changing billed units; keep unavailable prices unknown. Record URL, retrieval date, raw SHA-256, effective date and source kind. Test a valid response, a malformed or mismatched unit response, and an empty response. Promote through a versioned lock and preserve prior evidence. Run price-lock and reconciliation checks. Rebuild derived claims only after the source is reviewed; never edit the locked book by hand.

---
name: add-a-cost-rule
description: Add an allocation, ownership or waste rule to MLSpend and evaluate its accounting invariants against independent truth.
---

# Add A Cost Rule

Read AGENTS.md, evaluation/v2/plan.json and the relevant method module. Consume observed telemetry or contracted marts only; never import sealed truth into a method. State the economic assumption and the counterfactual action. Add tests for a valid nontrivial case, an invariant-violating case and empty input. Preserve exact money totals and unknown denominators. Register a new study version before changing thresholds after holdout results are known. Have packages/evaluation grade the rule with independent reruns, report boundary failures and uncertainty, and regenerate claims from the manifest. Run the import-boundary gate and affected tests.

---
name: explain-a-bill
description: Explain a team bill or cost difference in MLSpend using the contracted marts and generated manifest, with every number traceable to evidence.
---

# Explain A Bill

Read AGENTS.md and results/expanded/manifest.json. Resolve the requested team, month, book and method; do not mix direct forecast spend with fully loaded statements. Read the matching allocation, units, idle and incident rows. Reconcile the team statement to its direct and shared parts and the full month to the source total. Compare policies using the same cost population. Link the generated statement and source digest. State simulated versus measured usage and shadow versus paid cost. Report unavailable inputs explicitly. Do not fetch fresh prices into a locked historical calculation or invent a cash-saving claim. Verify every quoted number against the manifest before responding.

allocation.intro: The same source total supports five policies. The capacity Shapley calculation enumerates every coalition; its normalized shares allocate the recorded shared bill.
allocation.limit: Capacity contribution is a fairness reference under this coalition cost model. It is not an objective fairness label. Namespace and network must agree before an untagged charge is assigned.
allocation.title: The method changes the statement.

anomalies.intro: Seasonal MAD and positive CUSUM are calibrated on development data with a false-alarm budget. Hourly and daily team, service and SKU series are scored on held-out months.
anomalies.limit: Zero-hour detections are boundary results from timestamped synthetic incidents, not evidence of zero production latency. Event recall and point precision answer different questions. Post-development SKUs with no calibration history are unscored.
anomalies.title: Find the sweep before the invoice.

commitments.intro: Capacity is selected on development demand using actual locked public offer rates. Held-out regret is relative to the best registered capacity with hindsight.
commitments.limit: Fractional perturbations are analytical sensitivity points, not necessarily purchasable units. No commitment was purchased. Future demand and provider offer availability can change.
commitments.title: Buy the floor, measure the regret.

data.intro: Locked public snapshot applied to a simulated calendar; never represented as a historical invoice
data.limit: FOCUS uses typed contracts and supplemental normative checks. The official validator's latest rule set contains a dependency cycle, and older rules contain documented contradictions. The raw official report is retained; full official certification is not claimed.
data.title: Follow the number back.

estimate.intro: Compare hosting classes and token components using caller-supplied throughput. A live estimate is saved before its response; offline calculations are visibly labeled.
estimate.limit: A size class filters plausible options; it is not a memory-fit, latency or quality benchmark. Storage and network are excluded from this workload estimate.
estimate.title: Price the capacity you need.

forecast.intro: Seasonal naive, trend-seasonal and gradient boosting compete only on development history. Daily and monthly rolling-origin predictions are evaluated separately; intervals use earlier residuals.
forecast.limit: Team forecasts use direct spend, while statements include shared allocation. Serial dependence can invalidate nominal conformal coverage. Inadequate monthly calibration produces an unavailable interval. Live future forecasts are kept separate from these synthetic backtests.
forecast.title: A forecast earns its interval.

playbook.intro: A practical review path for an engineering lead, finance partner or interviewer.
playbook.limit: Review the limitations beside each method. A recommendation is an experiment to validate, not authorization to change an unrelated production system.

rows: Source records and four-grain count/cost reconciliation
Stop if count or currency differs
Check whether a node can actually be removed
Use visibly local calculation when unavailable
Never assume a timed-out POST failed

playbook.title: Use the bill to make a decision.

portfolio.intro: Public Actions jobs include every attempt in the recorded window. Committed ledgers preserve measured output and token counts. Unknown prices remain unknown.
portfolio.limit: These are measured public records at shadow prices. Runner-contained work is not charged twice. Missing GPU ledgers, unknown NIM token rates and unmatched Databricks SKUs prevent a complete total. Undated answer evaluations are excluded from the window. No per-refresh or per-answer total is invented from unrelated CI jobs.

sections.note: Job minutes round up individually. Public Linux runner usage is priced at the private paid equivalent; this is not an actual payment.

recommendations.intro: Each action is estimated from observed telemetry, then independently rerun against the whole simulated platform. Shared-capacity effects can reduce savings or increase cost.
recommendations.limit: Joint saving comes from one combined rerun. Incident-removal effects and standalone action savings are not additive; no summed savings claim. The avoidable reference combines registered actions and incident removal; it is not a proof of the global optimum. Resampled estimate intervals are not guaranteed cash-saving intervals. Model switching requires the registered quality floor.
recommendations.title: Free capacity is not cash saved.

report.intro: Read the statement, inspect what a policy moves, then test whether an intervention changes the total bill. The registered hypotheses below do not establish superiority.
report.limit: This independent replication was registered after earlier version results were already known. The added long-term contract is a documented completeness correction. Simulated effects are not production savings. Created for Ajay Mekala with AI assistance.

sections.note: Negative favors the registered method. Teams are the resampling clusters. The correction family contains the registered allocation and forecast comparisons.
sections.title: Registered comparisons

report.title: Cost ownership is a set of choices.

statement.intro: A simulated ML platform at a locked public price snapshot. Usage is the allocation method of record. Idle capacity is visible before distribution.
statement.limit: This is a synthetic platform, not a provider invoice. Later public prices are applied to an earlier simulated calendar; credits, tax and negotiated discounts are excluded.

sections.note: USD effective cost. Purchase cash and amortized consumption are reconciled separately.
sections.title: The monthly statement · 2025-12

statement.title: Every dollar has an owner.

unit.intro: Direct prediction, answer, training and notebook models receive each owner statement in proportion to direct cost. Shared support is allocated once; no denominator is invented for idle notebooks. Marginal inference uses simulated throughput of 18000 requests per node-hour.
unit.limit: The throughput conversion and model quality scores are simulator assumptions. A zero next-batch cost means the next batch fits the reserved capacity. A zero denominator is not reported as a free output.
unit.title: One prediction has two prices.

statement: mlspend is a portfolio demonstration. Its platform costs are simulated with known truth. Its portfolio costs are shadow estimates of public project usage at published list prices; nobody paid these amounts. No figure is a quote, an invoice or financial advice.
